title: Beyond Ideological Blocs: The ICDPP’s New Intercontinental Political Dialogue
gist: In September 2026 a new Inter-Continental Dialogue among Political Parties (ICDPP) launched in Seoul with 23 parties from 23 countries (19 governing, four opposition) spanning Asia, Africa, the Americas and Europe. The forum, linked to ICAPP chair Chung Eui-yong, positions itself as cross-ideological party-to-party diplomacy.

insights.claim: A new forum, the Inter-Continental Dialogue among Political Parties (ICDPP), was launched in Seoul in September 2026, gathering political leaders from Asia, Africa, the Americas and Europe.
insights.speaker: Kenichi Suzuki
insights.so_what: Emergence of new non-Western-led multilateral political networks may shape future alignment outside traditional blocs.
insights.quote: In September 2026, political leaders and party representatives from Asia, Africa, the Americas, and Europe gathered in Seoul to launch a new forum

insights.claim: The ICDPP's inaugural meeting in Seoul brought together 23 political parties from 23 countries, 19 of them governing parties and four in opposition.
insights.speaker: Kenichi Suzuki
insights.so_what: Heavy weighting toward governing parties gives the forum a direct channel into sitting governments rather than being a talking shop for opposition figures.
insights.quote: The inaugural meeting brought together 23 political parties from 23 countries, including 19 governing and four opposition parties.

insights.claim: The ICDPP participant list mixes ideologically disparate actors, including Ethiopia's ruling Prosperity Party, Pakistan Muslim League, a Hungarian European Conservatives group chair, the Dominican Republic's País Posible, and Japan's opposition Constitutional Democratic Party, consistent with its framing as a dialogue beyond ideological blocs.
insights.speaker: Kenichi Suzuki
insights.so_what: Cross-ideological party networks could become informal channels for Global South and middle-power coordination.

insights.claim: The ICDPP builds on existing regional party networks: it is associated with Chung Eui-yong, chair of the ICAPP Standing Committee and former South Korean foreign minister, and includes a vice president of Latin America's COPPPAL.
insights.speaker: Kenichi Suzuki
insights.so_what: South Korea is using party-level diplomacy as a soft-power tool to convene intercontinental networks.
insights.quote: Chung Eui-yong, chair of the Standing Committee of the International Conference of Asian Political Parties (ICAPP) and former South Korean foreign minister
